title: 2023 AMC 12B Problem 20
statement: Cyrus the frog jumps \(2\) units in a direction, then \(2\) more in another direction. What is the probability that he lands less than \(1\) unit away from his starting position?

solutions.text:
Take the first jump as \((2,0)\) and the second as \((2\cos\theta,2\sin\theta)\) with \(\theta\) uniform on \([0,2\pi).\) The landing distance satisfies \(R^2=(2+2\cos\theta)^2\) \(+(2\sin\theta)^2\) \(=8+8\cos\theta.\) We need \(R\lt 1,\) i.e. \(\cos\theta\lt-\tfrac78.\) The measure of such angles is \(2\arccos\tfrac78,\) so the probability is \(\dfrac{2\arccos\tfrac78}{2\pi}= \dfrac{\arccos\tfrac78}{\pi}.\) Using \(\arccos(1-2x^2)=2\arcsin x\) with \(x=\tfrac14\) gives \(\arccos\tfrac78=2\arcsin\tfrac14,\) so the probability is \(\dfrac{2\arcsin\tfrac14}{\pi}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Fix the first jump along the \(x\)-axis; the second jump makes a uniformly random angle \(\theta\)
